title: Uniform bound on all chart residue transcendence degrees after arbitrary base change
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Use chartwise local finite type and local finite presentation [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact, with quasi-compact diagonal. A module of finite type is locally finitely generated on etale scheme charts; a finitely presented module has locally an exact presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to M\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Let $Y$ be an affine scheme and $f:X\to Y$ a finite type morphism of algebraic spaces with quasi-compact diagonal. There exists an integer $D\geq0$ such that for every scheme $B\to Y$, every representable etale scheme chart $a:U\to X\times_YB$, and every $u\in U$ with image $v\in B$, one has $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(v)}\kappa(u)\leq D$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Empty fibres impose no condition. The same $D$ works for all $B$ and all charts, which need not be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0CX1 (theorem-flat-dimension-n-representable), proof, paragraph beginning “In particular the situation is local”: bounded fibre dimensions over an affine base, combined with chartwise transcendence degrees in Tag 0CWS.

proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$. The quasi-compactness in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], tested on the identity of the affine target, says that $|X|$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] to choose a representable surjective etale atlas $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$. The composite $W\to Y$ is locally of finite type by the chart test in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], using the identity chart of $Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $A$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by finitely many elements $a_1,\ldots,a_D$. Fix this $D\geq0$ before making any base change. If $X$ is empty, take the empty atlas, $A=0$, and $D=0$.

Let $B\to Y$ be arbitrary and $w\in W_B=W\times_Y B$ lie over $v\in B$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq B$ of $v$, represented by a prime $\mathfrak p\subset C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $w$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A\otimes_R C$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. The localization and residue-field formulas of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] give $\kappa(w)=\operatorname{Frac}((A\otimes_R C)/\mathfrak q)$: localization inverts precisely the nonzero elements of this domain. In this field the copy of $C/\mathfrak p$ extends to its fraction field $\kappa(v)$. Every tensor is a polynomial in the images $\bar a_i$ with coefficients in $C$, so $\kappa(w)=\kappa(v)(\bar a_1,\ldots,\bar a_D)$. Set $s=\{\bar a_1,\ldots,\bar a_D\}$. Every element is $x/y$ with $x,y\in\kappa(v)[s]$ and $y\ne0$, hence satisfies the nonzero polynomial $yT-x$. Thus [lem-sfb-algebraic-adjoin-transcendence-bound] applies to the field $\kappa(w)$ over $\kappa(v)$ and yields $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(v)}\kappa(w)\leq |s|\leq D$. This calculation uses no finite type assumption on $C$ or $B$.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); Tag 030F (lemma-transcendence-degree), generating-set argument, with its cited Mathlib ring generalization.

proof.text: Now fix an arbitrary representable etale chart $U\to X_B$ and $u\in U$ over $v$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], the base-changed atlas $W_B\to X_B$ is surjective etale. The scheme $T=U\times_{X_B}W_B$ therefore has etale projections $T\to U$ and $T\to W_B$, and the first is surjective. Choose $t\in T$ above $u$, with image $w\in W_B$. Both $w$ and $u$ map to $v$. Restrict each projection to an affine neighbourhood of $t$ inside the inverse image of an affine neighbourhood of its image. Its affine ring map is etale by the affine-chart characterization in [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] to these two ring maps. It gives finite separable, in particular algebraic, extensions $\kappa(t)/\kappa(u)$ and $\kappa(t)/\kappa(w)$. All residue maps commute with the structural map from $\kappa(v)$ because the square is a fibre product.

source.place: Sheaf fibre products and representable etale base change; Tags 02GI (definition-etale) and 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), part (2).

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] to $\kappa(v)\subseteq\kappa(u)\subseteq\kappa(t)$ and to $\kappa(v)\subseteq\kappa(w)\subseteq\kappa(t)$. The two algebraic upper extensions have transcendence degree zero, so $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(v)}\kappa(u)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(v)}\kappa(t)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(v)}\kappa(w)\leq D$ by step 2. The atlas and its generators were chosen before $B$, $U$ and $u$, so this is the required uniform bound. Empty fibres have no points to check, and no quasi-compactness of $U$ was used.

Source: Stacks 0CX1 (spaces-flat l.2027-2030) asserts bounded fibre dimension without proof, and the split supplies that bound in chart form (0CWS). Step tags 03H6, 01T2, 01I4, 030F and 02GL checked in tags/tags. Step 1: def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli defines quasi-compactness by pulling back along affines, which on id_Y gives |X| quasi-compact. lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas then gives an affine atlas Spec A. The chart test with b = id_Y makes Spec A -> Y locally of finite type, and lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs gives A finitely generated over R. D is fixed before B is chosen. Step 2: Spec(A⊗C) is open in W_B, κ(w) = κ(v)(ā_i), and yT - x gives algebraicity over κ(v)[s]. The Mathlib leaf trdeg_le_cardinalMk then gives trdeg ≤ D, with no finiteness assumed on C. Step 3: W_B ≅ W×_X X_B is surjective étale by lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers. T = U×W_B is a scheme with T->U surjective and T->W_B étale (def-trf-algebraic-space). The affine restrictions are étale ring maps, and the étale residue-field lemma makes κ(t) algebraic over both κ(u) and κ(w), all compatibly over κ(v). Step 4: the tower formula gives equality of the transcendence degrees. Edge cases tested: empty X or B, affine d-space (D = d, sharp), non-Noetherian C, non-quasi-compact charts.
